note: The vendor registry. Each target declares its runtime, how it is deployed, and the idiomatic endpoint it maps every scenario to. 'kind' = self-host (run through our identical rig, fully comparable) vs hosted (runs on the vendor's own infra; context only, never in a 'measured on the reference host' column). harness/k6/scenario.js and tools/generate-report.mjs both read this file.

reference.hostSpec: Intel Core Ultra 5 125H (18 threads), 32 GB RAM, NVMe, Ubuntu 26.04, Docker 29.8
reference.database: PostgreSQL 16, one container per target on the same host
reference.staticHost: Every figure in the head-to-head, the static metrics and the S01 to S05 latencies alike, was measured on this one rig, each target and its own PostgreSQL side by side, so the A/B is valid. The load generator runs on the same machine. No figure here comes from the Hetzner reference host. The sustained-throughput rows stay targets until that sweep runs.

targets.name: LyEve
targets.imageNote: The column is measured on a tagged release, the published image as it ships, so anyone can pull the same bytes. Re-measuring a new release means naming its tag in LYEVE_IMAGE (or here) and running the sweep again. The run date is recorded with every result.

pendingNotes.S05: the free tier allows five logins per fifteen minutes per address and refuses the rest with 429. Changing the limit needs a license

targets.readyNote: /readyz is a probe and can answer before the application does; /api/admin/setup answers 503 until the engine serves, so cold start is timed against it.
targets.notes: Every plugin compiled into one binary, activated per license; with no license the free baseline starts. No subprocess, no CDN plugin fetch.

targets.name: Strapi
targets.imageNote: Strapi v4/v5 does not ship a canonical runtime image; the harness builds one from a pinned create-strapi-app via harness/compose/strapi.yml.

pendingNotes.S05: the stock users-permissions plugin rate-limits /api/auth/local and refuses the burst with 429

targets.notes: REST via the content-type API; auth via users-permissions plugin.

targets.name: Directus
targets.notes: Official image. REST via the items API; auth returns access + refresh tokens.

targets.name: Payload
targets.imageNote: Payload is a framework embedded in a Node/Next app; the harness builds a minimal pinned app via harness/compose/payload.yml.
targets.notes: REST auto-generated per collection; auth on the users collection.
